notes: AUDITABLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every exchange session this platform generates. Downstream code
(coverage denominators, gap detection, and the Phase 4 leakage firewall's feature cutoffs) is
validated AGAINST the sessions produced from this file, so a wrong entry here is invisible by
construction. Read it as data, not as an implementation detail: every field is meant to be
checkable against a published exchange calendar by a human, without reading any C#.
WHAT IS A RULE AND WHAT IS DATA. Only the statutory, mechanically-defined holidays are rules
(nth-weekday, fixed-date-with-weekend-observance, Good Friday from the Gregorian Easter
computation). EVERYTHING an exchange decided rather than derived is data: unscheduled closures
(9/11, Hurricane Sandy, national days of mourning), unscheduled early closes, the year a holiday
entered the calendar (MLK 1998, Juneteenth 2022), and every early-close wall-clock time. A purely
rule-based generator invents sessions on days the market was shut; that is the specific defect
this split exists to prevent.
CONFIDENCE. Every unscheduled entry carries a `confidence`. 'high' = widely documented and
cross-checkable; 'medium' = documented but the venue-by-venue detail is inferred; 'unverified' =
believed correct but NOT confirmed against a published exchange calendar — grep for it and check
it before trusting any study whose window includes that date.
BUMP generatorVersion ON ANY CHANGE to this file. SessionGenerator.GeneratorVersion must match it
(a unit test enforces this), and research.sessions.generator_version records it per row, so a
regenerated calendar is distinguishable from a stale one.
TIMES ARE EXCHANGE-LOCAL WALL CLOCK in the calendar's IANA time zone. They are never offsets.
SessionClock converts; nothing else in the platform is permitted to.

US_MARKET.name: New Year's Day
US_MARKET.note: Deliberately NOT saturdayToFriday. NYSE Rule 7.2 excepts New Year's Day from the Saturday rule: Jan 1 2005, Jan 1 2011 and Jan 1 2022 all fell on a Saturday and the preceding Fridays (Dec 31) were full trading days.

US_MARKET.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
US_MARKET.note: Not an NYSE/Cboe holiday before 1998 — the market traded on MLK Day 1993-1997. A rule without fromYear silently deletes five real January sessions.

US_MARKET.name: Good Friday
US_MARKET.note: Two days before Gregorian Easter Sunday (Meeus/Butcher). Verified against 2001-04-13, 2012-04-06, 2024-03-29, 2025-04-18, 2026-04-03.

US_MARKET.name: Juneteenth National Independence Day
US_MARKET.note: First observed 2022-06-20 (Jun 19 2022 was a Sunday). The market was open on Jun 18 2021.

US_MARKET.name: Day before Independence Day
US_MARKET.note: July 3, but only when July 4 itself falls Mon-Fri (so July 3 is neither a weekend nor the observed holiday). Matches 2013/2014/2017/2018/2019/2023/2024/2025 early closes and the absence of one in 2015/2016/2020/2021/2022.

US_MARKET.name: Christmas Eve
US_MARKET.note: Dec 24, only when Dec 25 falls Mon-Fri. Matches the 2012-2015, 2018-2020, 2024, 2025 early closes and the absence of one in 2016, 2017, 2021-2023.

CBOE.note: Cboe follows the NYSE holiday and unscheduled-closure schedule, including both Hurricane Sandy days. The 1997-10-27 circuit-breaker close applied to Cboe too, but the exact Cboe index-option halt time is not recorded here, so no unscheduled early close is asserted — an unasserted early close leaves a normal-length session, which shows up as a visible low-coverage afternoon rather than as silently discarded data.

CME.note: Differs from NYSE/Cboe on Hurricane Sandy: CME's electronic markets stayed open on 2012-10-29 and 2012-10-30 while the NYSE and Cboe were shut, so those dates are absent from CME_UNSCHEDULED. The 1996 blizzard entry is likewise absent (a New York weather closure). Day-of-mourning handling for CME equity index is the least certain part of this file — see the per-entry confidence flags.

calendars.description: NYSE/ARCA cash equities regular session. SPY's calendar.
Cboe index options regular session (SPX, SPXW, VIX). Closes 15:15 CT = 16:15 ET — fifteen minutes after the cash equity close, on full and half days alike.

Cboe Global Trading Hours for SPX/SPXW/VIX options: 19:15 CT the PRIOR calendar day through 08:15 CT on the trading date (20:15-09:15 ET). effectiveFrom is the near-24x5 GTH expansion; before it no overnight index-option session existed, and generating one would manufacture sessions that never happened. The 19:15 CT open is runtime-verified — docs/research/ibkr-data-capability-matrix.md records useRTH=0 SPX bars starting 19:15 US/Central on the prior calendar day, and the 20:15-09:15 ET session in the pacing/limits section.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: appliesEarlyClose is false because a GTH session ENDS in the morning, before any afternoon early close could shorten it. An early close on trading date D truncates D's RTH, not D's GTH. Whether Cboe suppresses the overnight session on a holiday EVENING (which would remove the GTH session belonging to the next trading date) is not asserted here — see eveningSessionClosedOn.

calendars.description: CME Globex E-mini S&P 500. The Globex day for trading date D runs 17:00 CT on D-1 through 16:00 CT on D (recorded as the GTH row); RTH is the 08:30-15:15 CT equity-index regular session nested inside it. effectiveFrom is the ES contract launch.

sessions.label: GTH
sessions.note: Globex reopens at 17:00 CT on holiday evenings (e.g. the Christmas Day evening session belonging to Dec 26), so this row is generated whenever its TRADING DATE is a trading day, regardless of what the prior calendar day was. The 16:00-17:00 CT daily maintenance halt is the gap between one day's close and the next day's open, so it needs no separate representation.
